# Lab 1.4: Query Settings That Matter

## What We Are Going to Do
Try the result cache, batch priority, a destination table, and maximum bytes billed, from both the console and the CLI.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create a dataset for this module.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab01</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] See the cache.** Run the query from Lab 1.3 twice. On the second run, **Job information** shows **"Results cached"** and **Bytes billed: 0 B**.

3. **[Console] Change query settings.** Click **More → Query settings**:
   - Untick **Use cached results**.
   - Set **Destination** to `lab01.top_words`, with **Write if empty**.
   - Set **Job priority** to **Batch**.
   - Under **Advanced options**, set **Maximum bytes billed** to `50000000`.

   Click **Save** and **Run**. The result is written to `lab01.top_words`.

4. **[CLI] Same settings with bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --nouse_cache --batch \
  --destination_table=lab01.top_words --replace \
  --maximum_bytes_billed=50000000 \
  'SELECT word, SUM(word_count) AS total
   FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare` GROUP BY word'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[CLI] Hit the bytes limit on purpose.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --maximum_bytes_billed=1000 \
  'SELECT * FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare`'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The query fails with **"Query exceeded limit for bytes billed"**. Nothing is charged.

6. **[Console] Check the location setting.** In **Query settings → Location**, see that **Automatic location selection** picks `US` because the data is in `US`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Cached re-run | 0 bytes billed |
| Batch priority | Queued until slots are free (usually seconds) |
| Destination table | `lab01.top_words` created |
| Bytes limit | Query fails safely, nothing charged |
